title: OpenAI and Cisco release Shirudo, an eBPF runtime that shields unpatched Linux hosts
summary: OpenAI and Cisco open-sourced Shirudo, an eBPF-based runtime that attaches temporary shields to running Linux services, blocking a known exploit path before a vendor patch reaches every machine. In a controlled test, a shield written with OpenAI's Codex blocked a Java4Shell attempt against a live Elasticsearch process without a restart. Shirudo is published under BSD 2-Clause, its BPF programs are dual-licensed BSD and GPL, and Cisco's Isovalent describes the project as a rewrite of its Tetragon platform designed for agents.
